outcome: total quantity of opioid medications prescribed at discharge
proportion of prescriptions with a duration of longer than 5 days
cohort: 93,760 adult patients who received an opioid prescription at discharge after undergoing general, obstetric and gynecologic (obstetric/gynecologic), or orthopedic surgery
finding: The implementation of mandatory prescription drug monitoring program (PDMP) consultation with concurrent electronic health record (EHR)-based alerts was associated with an immediate decrease in opioid prescribing across general, obstetric/gynecologic, and orthopedic surgical specialties.
mod_finding: For cesarean delivery, the median number of opioid tablets prescribed decreased during the quarter of implementation, but median morphine milligram equivalents (MMEs) did not, whereas decreases were observed in both median MMEs and number of tablets prescribed for laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
